title: Attaining the maximum on the support of a probability mass function
statement: Let $\\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\\Omega$, and let $g:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ satisfy $g(x)\\le 1$ for every $x$. If the expectation of $g$ under $p$ is $1$, then $g(x)=1$ at every point with $p(x)\\ne 0$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a probability mass function on $\\Omega$
$g$ is real-valued and bounded above by $1$ at every point
The selected point has nonzero probability
